turn_text: Now both the state of Florida and the federal government are investigating the September 15th attack, and there was some concern expressed as a reason for that, that the feds might not be able to bring sufficient charges against the suspect. Well, I'll say that. So I am actually a former federal prosecutor and can tell you what happens there is very typical. So when this happened in the immediate hours after this attack in Palm Beach, federal prosecutors needed to bring a charge immediately. And what those done charges that they brought in the first instance are relatively simple charges. easy to prove the evidence for those charges was readily there. So they were able to bring an immediate charge and keep them held in custody and have now brought a superseding indictment with more complex charges. So this was not an unusual thing. I fully expected from the outset that the federal criminal case would ultimately include these types of charges. It just allowed them a few days to gather the additional evidence about who this person was and what he was doing so that they could bring that more comprehensive charging document against this defendant. So thus far for us, The Secret Service has been working with us, has been briefing us, has been for the health task force, has been forthcoming with the information that we have been requesting from them. But there's still a long way to go. We have a lot of questions still about who these assailants are, how they got to this place. Were they working alone? So those are the types of questions that a lot of that frankly lies with the FBI.
